dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:201.text: Coral, 珊瑚. Formed from 玉, with 胡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:202.text: A lustrous stone called 璧𤥗, found among the western Hu peoples. Formed from 玉, with 戼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:203.text: Jade placed in the mouth when sending off the dead. Formed from 玉 and 含; 含 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:204.text: Jade presented as a funerary gift to the dead. Formed from 玉, with 𣣸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:205.text: Fine metal, the same color as jade. Formed from 玉, with 湯 indicating the sound. The Rites says: “For feudal lords' worn knives, the upper fitting is 璗 and the lower 璆.”

shuowen:206.text: A 𩆜 shaman, who serves the spirits with jade. Formed from 玉, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:207.text: A woman's head ornament. Formed from 玉, with 加 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “A headdress and hairpin with six 珈.”

shuowen:208.text: A kind of ring. Formed from 玉, with 豦 indicating the sound. It appears in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

shuowen:209.text: A jade drinking cup. The Xia called it 琖, the Yin 斚, and the Zhou 爵. Formed from 玉, with 戔 indicating the sound; alternatively formed from 皿.

shuowen:210.text: A treasure. Formed from 玉, with abbreviated 深 indicating the sound.

shuowen:211.text: An ornate decoration. Formed from 玉, with 當 indicating the sound.

shuowen:212.text: Five hundred pearls. Formed from 玉, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:213.text: Jade. Formed from 玉, with 可 indicating the sound.

shuowen:214.text: Jade. Formed from 玉, with 己 indicating the sound.

shuowen:215.text: Jade. Formed from 玉, with 羽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:216.text: 璀璨: the brilliance of jade. Formed from 玉, with 崔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:217.text: The brilliance of jade. Formed from 玉, with 粲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:218.text: Jade. Formed from 玉, with 叔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:219.text: A jade disc six inches across. Formed from 玉, with 宣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:220.text: Jade. Formed from 玉, with 共 indicating the sound.

shuowen:221.text: Two pieces of jade joined into one 𤤴. All characters in the 𤤴 category are formed from 𤤴.

shuowen:222.text: To divide a ceremonial jade. Formed from 𤤴 and 刀.

shuowen:223.text: A leather case between a carriage's rails. In antiquity an envoy carrying jade stored it there. Formed from 車 and 𤤴. Pronounced the same as 服.

shuowen:224.text: Cloud vapor. A pictograph. All characters in the 气 category are formed from 气.

shuowen:225.text: Portentous vapor. Formed from 气, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:226.text: A person entrusted with affairs or duties. Numbers begin at one and end at ten. Formed from 一 and 十. Confucius is quoted as saying: “To bring ten together under one is to make 士.” All characters in the 士 category are formed from 士.

shuowen:227.text: A husband. Formed from 士, with 胥 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The woman did not err; the man was double in his conduct.” 士 here means husband. Pronounced the same as 細.

shuowen:228.text: Great or strong. Formed from 士, with 爿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:229.text: To dance. Formed from 士, with 尊 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Dance for me, 墫墫.”

shuowen:230.text: To pass through above and below. Drawn upward, it is pronounced like 囟; drawn downward, like 𨓆. All characters in the 丨 category are formed from 丨.

shuowen:231.text: Inside. Formed from 口; 丨 passes through above and below.

shuowen:232.text: The appearance of a banner pole. Formed from 丨 and 㫃; 㫃 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:233.text: Plants first sprouting. It depicts a 丨 emerging, with branches and stem. Ancient writing sometimes uses it for 艸. Read like 徹. All characters in the 屮 category are formed from 屮. This explanation is Yin Tong's.

shuowen:234.text: Difficulty. It depicts plants first sprouting, struggling with difficulty. Formed from 屮 piercing 一; 一 is the earth, and the tail is curved. The Changes says: “屯: the firm and yielding first join, and birth is difficult.”

shuowen:235.text: Plants growing luxuriantly upward. Formed from 屮, with 母 indicating the sound.

shuowen:236.text: Abundance or intensity; the text links the meaning to harmful plants growing prolifically. The received graphic formula says “formed from 屮 and 毒”; Duan instead analyzes 屮 as the plant component and 毒 as the phonetic. [Received graphical formula is self-referential and disputed.]

shuowen:237.text: Plants first sprouting, their fragrance spreading. Formed from 屮 and 分; 分 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:238.text: 菌𡴆, ground mushrooms growing in clusters in fields. Formed from 屮, with 六 indicating the sound.

shuowen:239.text: Smoke rising from fire. Formed from 屮 and 黑; 屮黑 means to blacken with smoke.

shuowen:240.text: The many plants. Formed from two 屮. All characters in the 艸 category are formed from 艸.

shuowen:241.text: The reigning sovereign's taboo personal name.

shuowen:242.text: What grows on trees is 果; what grows on the ground is 蓏. Formed from 艸 and 㼌.

shuowen:243.text: A divine plant. Formed from 艸 and 之.

shuowen:244.text: 萐莆, an auspicious plant. In Yao's time it grew in the kitchen, fanning away summer heat to make it cool. Formed from 艸, with 疌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:245.text: The plant 萐莆. Formed from 艸, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:246.text: Red seedlings, a fine grain. Formed from 艸, with 釁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:247.text: Small beans. Formed from 艸, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:248.text: Bean stalks. Formed from 艸, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:249.text: Young beans. Formed from 艸, with 靃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:250.text: The name of the fruit of 鹿藿. Formed from 艸, with 狃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:251.text: Grain or millet shoots that emerge but fail to mature are called 蕫蓈. Formed from 艸, with 郎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:252.text: The weed 莠 grows beneath grain and millet. Formed from 艸, with 秀 indicating the sound. Read like 酉.

shuowen:253.text: Hemp seed. Formed from 艸, with 肥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:254.text: A female, seed-bearing hemp plant. Formed from 艸, with 子 indicating the sound. Another explanation uses 芓 as equivalent to 枲, hemp.

shuowen:255.text: The hemp plant 芓. Formed from 艸, with 異 indicating the sound.

shuowen:256.text: 桂荏, the plant perilla. Formed from 艸, with 穌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:257.text: 桂荏, namely 蘇, perilla. Formed from 艸, with 任 indicating the sound.

shuowen:258.text: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 矢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:259.text: An excellent vegetable: the 䔇 of Yunmeng. Formed from 艸, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:260.text: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 癸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:261.text: A vegetable that wards off dampness. Formed from 艸, with 彊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:262.text: A pungent vegetable, 薔虞. Formed from 艸, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:263.text: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 祖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:264.text: A vegetable resembling perilla. Formed from 艸, with 豦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:265.text: A vegetable resembling bean leaves. Formed from 艸, with 微 indicating the sound.

shuowen:266.text: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 唯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:267.text: A vegetable resembling mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 近 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou has “pickled 菦.”

shuowen:268.text: A vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 釀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:269.text: The vegetable amaranth. Formed from 艸, with 見 indicating the sound.

shuowen:270.text: Large leaves and a substantial root startle people, hence it is called 芌. Formed from 艸, with 亏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:271.text: In Qi, 芌 is called 莒. Formed from 艸, with 呂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:272.text: The plant 蘧麥. Formed from 艸, with 遽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:273.text: 大菊, namely 蘧麥. Formed from 艸, with 匊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:274.text: A strong-smelling vegetable. Formed from 艸, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:275.text: 蘘荷, also called 葍蒩. Formed from 艸, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:276.text: Chive flowers. Formed from 艸, with 青 indicating the sound.

shuowen:277.text: 蘆菔, radish. Another explanation: the root of 薺. Formed from 艸, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:278.text: 蘆菔, resembling turnip, with seeds like small beans. Formed from 艸, with 服 indicating the sound.

shuowen:279.text: Duckweed: rootless, growing afloat on water. Formed from 艸, with 平 indicating the sound.

shuowen:280.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 臣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:281.text: Large duckweed. Formed from 艸, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:282.text: A plant used to dye blue. Formed from 艸, with 監 indicating the sound.

shuowen:283.text: A plant that makes people forget sorrow. Formed from 艸, with 憲 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Where can I find 藼 grass?”

shuowen:284.text: 𦵡藭, a fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 宮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:285.text: The fragrant plant 𦵡藭. Formed from 艸, with 窮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:286.text: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 闌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:287.text: A plant from Wulin Mountain. Formed from 艸, with 姦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:288.text: A kind of 䕬 that can perfume the mouth. Formed from 艸, with 俊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:289.text: 芄蘭, namely 莞. Formed from 艸, with 丸 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Branches of 芄蘭.”

shuowen:290.text: Called 蘺 in Chu, 虈 in Jin, and 茝 in Qi. Formed from 艸, with 嚻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:291.text: 江蘺, namely 蘼蕪. Formed from 艸, with 離 indicating the sound.

shuowen:292.text: The plant 虈. Formed from 艸, with 𦣞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:293.text: The plant 蘪蕪. Formed from 艸, with 麋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:294.text: A fragrant plant. Formed from 艸, with 熏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:295.text: Water 萹茿. Formed from 艸 and 水, with 毒 indicating the sound. Read like 督.

shuowen:296.text: The plant 萹茿. Formed from 艸, with 扁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:297.text: The plant 萹茿. Formed from 艸, with abbreviated 筑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:298.text: The plant 芞輿. Formed from 艸, with 楬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:299.text: The plant 芞輿. Formed from 艸, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:300.text: The plant 馬苺. Formed from 艸, with 母 indicating the sound.
